title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD, Design Spec, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes - 2027-07
author: Olivia Chen
content:
Overview

Summary:
Redwood's Unified Inference product unifies the hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployment surfaces under a single developer experience and configurable runtime. This document consolidates the product overview, a concise PRD with requirements, a high-level design specification, roadmap & themes through Q3 2027, pricing and packaging guidance, and release notes for the 2027-07 release.

Audience:
- Product managers and engineering leads planning inference features
- Solutions engineers and customer success preparing migrations
- Sales and pricing for packaging and offers
- Engineering teams implementing runtime and ops workstreams

Goals:
1. Deliver a single API and configuration surface with consistent semantics across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
2. Reduce unit inference cost for typical web-scale NLP workloads by 20% through batching, caching, and quantization recommendations.
3. Provide first-class rollout controls (canary, A/B, automatic fallback) and observability that ties quality regressions to prompt sets and evals.
4. Ship the 2027-07 release with completed pricing tiers, client SDK updates, and migration guides.

Success metrics (12 months):
- Adoption: 60% of new hosted customers use Unified Inference config profiles within 3 months of signup.
- Cost: average tokens-per-dollar improvement of 18% for customers using recommended Optimize profiles.
- Reliability: maintain platform SLOs during rollout (see SLOs below).
- NPS/CSAT: mean CSAT >= 4.2 for migration support flows.

Product requirements (PRD):
(Format: MUST / SHOULD / NICE-TO-HAVE)

MUST:
- Single REST/SDK interface exposing text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking with identical request/response shapes across deployment modes.
- Configurable routing policies: latency-first, cost-first, regional-preference, and customer-tier.
- Rollout policies: per-route canary (0-20% traffic), weighted A/B, and automated fallback to compatible model variants.
- Runtime controls: batching window, KV cache TTL, quantization profile selection.
- Observability: per-route token cost, p50/p95/p99 latency, error breakdown, and prompt-set QA tracking.
- Security: audit logging, RBAC hooks, and KMS integrations for Private deployments.

SHOULD:
- UX: Console templates for common workloads (chat, summarization, search relevance).
- Smart defaults for batching and caching per model family.
- Integrated evals: ability to run prompt sets pre/post rollout and tie regressions to an alert.

NICE-TO-HAVE:
- Auto-apply quantization suggestions with simulated cost/quality estimates.
- Migration assistant that analyzes traffic and suggests configuration migration steps.

Requirements table (high level):
| ID | Area | Requirement | Owner | Acceptance Criteria | Priority |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---:|
| R-001 | API | Unified REST/SDK shapes for generation & embeddings | eng-platform | SDK tests pass, spec published | MUST |
| R-002 | Routing | Latency/cost/region policies | eng-serving-runtime | E2E routing test & perf benchmarks | MUST |
| R-003 | Rollouts | Canary/A-B/fallback controls | eng-platform | Console + API controls implemented | MUST |
| R-004 | Observability | Per-route cost/quality dashboards | eng-platform | Dashboards and alerts live | MUST |
| R-005 | Pricing | Tiered pricing + reserved capacity offers | finance-legal | Public pricing page + partner docs | MUST |

Design specification (high level):

Architecture components:
1. Control Plane (Console + API) - product-config-store, rollout-service, policy-engine. Owned by: eng-platform.
2. Serving Runtime - inference-engine, batcher, kv-cache, quantizer. Owned by: eng-serving-runtime.
3. Router - smart-router service for policy-based routing with fallback. Owned by: eng-platform.
4. Observability - metrics-store, tracing, cost-meter. Owned by: eng-platform + eng-sre.
5. Private Control Plane connector - secure sync for Private deployments (KMS + audit log forwarder). Owned by: eng-private-deployments.

Data flows (brief):
1. Client -> Unified API Gateway: validates request, extracts route tags.
2. Gateway -> Policy Engine: determines target model variant and deployment target (hosted/dedicated/private).
3. Gateway -> Batcher/Runtime: request assigned to a slot, KV cache consulted, inference executed, response streamed.
4. Observability hooks emit token/cost metrics and traces; evals service receives sampled prompts for QA.

API & config examples:
- Sample request (generation):
{
  "model": "redwood-unified-gpt-1.1",
  "deployment_mode": "auto",
  "policy": "latency-first",
  "max_tokens": 256,
  "stream": true
}

- Example rollout config (YAML):
route: user-chat-inbox
policy:
  type: canary
  stages:
    - name: initial
      weight: 5
    - name: ramp
      weight: 50
    - name: main
      weight: 100
fallback:
  to_variant: redwood-unified-gpt-1.0

Operational controls & runbook summary:
- Canary cadence: 24h at 5% -> 48h at 50% -> promote to 100% if no quality/regression alerts.
- Automatic rollback: trigger if p95 latency > target by 30% OR error_rate > 0.5% OR eval-quality drop > 2 points over baseline.
- Owners: Product owner (Olivia Chen), Runtime lead (Diego Morales), Observability lead (Tina Park).

SLOs and thresholds (applies to hosted endpoints by default):
- Availability: 99.95% monthly
- Latency: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 260ms, p99 < 600ms for "small" models (<= 4k tokens), adjusted per model family.
- Error budget: < 0.05% client-facing errors (4xx/5xx combined)

Roadmap & themes (Q4 2026 — Q3 2027):
- Q4 2026: Unified API v1 GA (text + embeddings), initial rollout controls, billing primitives.
- Q1 2027: Dedicated autoscaling policies, prefix KV caching, quantization profile catalog v1.
- Q2 2027: Console templates, integrated evals alerting, model routing policy enhancements (cost-aware fallbacks).
- Q3 2027: Private control plane v1, automated quantization suggestions, pricing/reserved-capacity offers finalized (this release).

Pricing & packaging notes (guidance for offers):
Principles:
- Clear tradeoffs: expose cost/latency tradeoffs per model family in Console.
- Two primary surfaces: Hosted usage-based + Dedicated reserved capacity.
- Enterprise add-ons: observability retention, compliance packs, premium SLAs.

Starter published pricing (public guidance):
| Tier | Surface | Invoice unit | Public list price (USD) | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| Pay-as-you-go | Hosted | per-1k prompt+completion tokens | $0.018 | baseline model family (redwood-unified-gpt-small) |
| Developer | Hosted | per-1k tokens + free trials | $0.012 | includes 3 seats, 14 day trial credits |
| Dedicated | Reserved capacity | monthly committed vGPU-hour | $X.XX* | custom sizing; includes SLA |
| Enterprise | Private | platform + support | custom | 12/24 month contracts, includes VPC connector |

*Dedicated pricing is customized; finance will publish a sizing calculator linking throughput and committed hours.

Cost controls & recommendations (for solutions teams):
- Default to cost-first policy for high-volume non-interactive workloads (embeddings batches, offline rerank).
- Use latency-first policy for interactive experiences; pair with small-model families and aggressive caching.
- Offer customers quantified estimates in Console: cost-per-1M-tokens and expected p95 latency by model and profile.

Release notes: 2027-07-05 (Unified Inference Release v2027-07)
Summary:
This release completes the pricing & packaging pieces of Unified Inference, adds the Private control plane v1 beta, and ships integrated evals alerts and Console templates. Key user-facing changes are listed below.

Highlights:
1. Pricing & Packaging: Public pricing page published; Reserved capacity offer and sizing calculator v1 live. (Owner: Finance & Product)
2. Console: New templates for Chat, Summarization, and Search Relevance; rollout config UI for canaries and weighted routing. (Owner: UX & Eng Platform)
3. Private control plane v1 (beta): secure connector, KMS integration, and audit forwarding. (Owner: Eng Private Deployments)
4. Observability: prompt-set QA alerts, cost-per-route dashboards, and token-level tracing. (Owner: Eng Platform + Eng SRE)
5. Runtime: KV prefix cache improvements (TTL controls) and quantization profile support in runtime options. (Owner: Eng Serving Runtime)

Bug fixes and internal changes:
- Fixed an edge-case where streaming responses could duplicate tokens during retry.
- Improved routing decisions for mixed-length requests to avoid latency cliffs.

Rollout plan (operational):
1. Staged deploy to canary infra: 48h smoke tests; route-level 5% traffic for critical routes.
2. Monitor SLOs and eval alerts for 72h.
3. Ramp to 50% over 48h conditional on no alerts.
4. Full promotion and public announcement after 7 days of stable metrics.

Migration guidance for customers:
- Hosted customers: no action needed for default behavior; opt-in to new pricing tiers or cost-first policies via Console.
- Dedicated customers: coordinate with Customer Success for sizing adjustments; reserved-capacity contracts will be amended for new pricing cadence.
- Private customers: Private control plane is beta; customers must schedule a migration window and provide KMS details.

- SDK changes: new "policy" and "deployment_mode" parameters added; backward compatible defaults preserve existing behavior.
- QA suite: regression-evals repo contains prompt sets used for pre-release checks; CI runs include performance benchmarks against nightly binaries.
